prompt:
Generate one high-quality cinematic 16:9 image for the specified section, not a generic slide or dashboard. No letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, arrows, diagrams, interface, checkmarks, traffic-light statuses or readable documents. The compositor adds every semantic mark independently. Do not invent a completed publication, a live security test, a solved outing, approval or consensus. Fictional editorial staging, not documentary evidence. Rich material detail, carefully controlled light, credible objects and hands. Keep designated annotation zones visually quiet. Never fill quiet zones with invented panels. Reference images establish cast and room identity only; follow this section's camera and blocking.
VISUAL FORMAT: dispatcher-cross-section
TEACHING PURPOSE: Locate the proposed component that can stop an effect.
CAMERA: Symmetrical low-angle cutaway through a physical boundary.
A dark cinematic cutaway of an abstract industrial access chamber: a single heavy brushed-steel partition at the horizontal CENTER, narrow warm slit of light, empty space to either side. Hardware is confined to the LOWER THIRD; the UPPER TWO THIRDS are clear charcoal haze for a three-node exact SVG circuit. Not science-fiction spectacle, no screens, no arrows, no status lamps, no actual movement or open gate. Make the boundary feel physical and inspectable without implying any live enforcement.
COMPOSITING INTENT: An agent-to-dispatcher-to-effect route spans the scene; a tall boundary at the dispatcher owns the credential. The moving request stops before the effect segment.
SEMANTIC AUTHORITY FOR CONTEXT ONLY, NEVER RENDER THESE WORDS: PROPOSED DESIGN / NOT LIVE PROOF. The proposed dispatcher owns the effect credential. It checks the protected grant before dispatch. The agent cannot edit that grant or acquire the credential. Unavailable authorization means hold. This is the trust boundary to build and test, not evidence that SideFX already enforces it.
